title: Formal verification example (authored)
description: What a person writes for one example: the change, why it matters, and what the verifier should conclude. Everything the verifier produces lives in result.json, generated by examples/tools/build.py.

id.description: Three-digit number, equal to the folder prefix.

title.description: What happens, in one line. Shown in the table of contents.

summary.description: Two or three sentences for a reader skimming the table of contents.

categories.description: What kind of breaking change the example is about.

severity.description: How bad it would be if the change shipped unnoticed. 'none' for changes that are safe.

file.description: Repo-relative path of the changed source file.

id.description: Approach ID in examples/approaches.md, for example B8.

kind.description: What the developer thought they were doing.

behaviourChangeIntended.description: True if the developer meant to change behaviour, and so regenerates the contract.

description.description: The change in the developer's words, and why it looked right.

patch.description: Unified diff against the repo, relative to this folder.

intendedInputs.description: For approach B9: a Java boolean expression over the method's parameters that describes the inputs the developer means to change, for example `seats >= 8`. The verifier proves that every other input behaves as before.

risk.description: What could go wrong in production if this change shipped unnoticed.

verdict.description: The verdict the verifier must reach. The generator fails if it does not.

explanation.description: Why the verdict is right, and how the verifier reached it.

resolution.description: What the developer should do next.

provenance.description: Where the example came from: a real incident, a session, or constructed.
